text:
maria-chen: heads up — our secret scanner flagged what looks like an internal API token in a public repo (redwood-examples). snippet points to commit 4f3a2b in `tools/auth-demo`. likely pattern: rw_internal_v1_XXXXXXXX.

opsbot: Automated detection: public-repo-secret-scan job #4521 detected potential credential in repo redwood-examples at path tools/auth-demo/main.go (commit 4f3a2b). Rule: internal-token-regex-v2. Confidence: medium.

samir-kaur: ugh. do we know which token type? short-lived or long-lived?

maria-chen: pattern suggests internal ingestion token (used by dev-only metrics ingest). not sure TTL. i didn't pull the secret, scanner gave only the matched string.

security-oncall: I'm on it. first steps: (1) identify token id if possible, (2) revoke/rotate immediately if it's a valid credential, (3) audit last 30 days of usage, (4) check customer-facing impact, (5) comms. tagging @elaine-ng for telemetry query.

elaine-ng: running queries now. can you paste the matched substring? i need the token prefix to search logs.

maria-chen: here's the matched context (sanitized): ````
const defaultToken = "rw_internal_v1_abc123def456"
// TODO: replace before publishing
````

samir-kaur: that looks like a real token format. maria — did you push credentials accidentally or was it historical?

maria-chen: historical commit from Feb 2025, pre-oss cleanup. repo became public in Jan 2026 after we moved examples. i missed that stray constant.

security-oncall: OK. elaine — can you check ingestion logs for token `rw_internal_v1_abc123def456` (and any token starting with `rw_internal_v1_abc123`) across prod/staging for last 90 days? also check GEO/IP anomalies.

elaine-ng: running queries: `select timestamp, src_ip, endpoint from logs where auth_token like 'rw_internal_v1_abc123%' order by timestamp desc limit 200` — will update in ~10m.

opsbot: NOTE: we redacted commit contents in GH mirror. Actioned by opsbot at 1783509180.

security-oncall: simultaneously: samir — please prepare rotation plan for that token family. We need a single-command revoke and replacement in CI/CD. Use `rwctl auth revoke` and create a new short-lived token. Also add immediate firewall block for any unknown IPs.

samir-kaur: on it. proposed commands: ``rwctl auth revoke rw_internal_v1_abc123def456 --force`` and ``rwctl auth issue --scope=metrics:ingest --ttl=12h --label=rotated-202603``. will open a rotation PR to update demo config and redeploy.

elaine-ng: query results: 3 unique source IPs called ingest endpoints with that token between 2026-02-10 and 2026-02-18. one IP is within our GCP range (likely internal), two are from cloud provider ranges in eu-west-1. no customer data endpoints accessed; only metrics ingest endpoints.

security-oncall: good that customer endpoints weren't hit. still treat as compromise. elk logs show usage peaked with small bursts. preserving logs for forensics: snapshotting now.

jordan: i'm checking KMS usage and key access logs. any rotation we do should not require KMS key change, just token revocation. however, we should add an audit event: `auth.token.rotate` tied to KMS key id for visibility.

devsec-jen: also file-level steps: (1) create GH PR to remove the secret and perform force push to purge from history using `git filter-repo` or BFG, (2) coordinate with OSS team to schedule a repo re-publication window, (3) notify external scanners that we remediated.

maria-chen: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-examples/pull/99 — removes constant and updates README. includes `git-filter-repo` rewrite plan in PR description.

security-oncall: action checklist: revoke token (samir), rotate configs (samir + maria), log analysis done (elaine), KMS/audit annotation (jordan), GH history purge (devsec-jen), customer impact check (elaine), incident advisory draft (security). assign owners in ticket after rotation.

opsbot: security ticket #SE-2026-221 created: "public repo leaked internal ingestion token". Assignees: security-oncall, samir-kaur, devsec-jen.

samir-kaur: revoked token now: `rwctl auth revoke rw_internal_v1_abc123def456 --executed-by=samir-kaur` (1783509302). issuing replacement with 12h TTL and updating demo env vars.

elaine-ng: confirmed usage logs stop after revocation timestamp. one client from eu-west-1 attempted a call after revocation and got 401. captured IPs and saved to ticket.

security-oncall: please also update Audit Log retention to ensure we keep these events for 1 year per compliance ask. jordan — can you create an ACL change request to log all `auth.*` events to long-term storage?

jordan: will file infra change: `logpipe add-rule --pattern 'auth.*' --dest long-term-archive --owner eng-logging` — target deploy in next 48h.

devsec-jen: started GH history purge on the fork; note: we'll need to coordinate with the forks and update any CI tokens that might still reference the old commit SHA. also adding a pre-merge hook that blocks committed token-like literals.

maria-chen: quick Q — do we need to reach out to customers?

security-oncall: no customer data impacted and token used for internal metrics only; recommend internal advisory only. draft: short incident note + mitigation steps + proactive monitoring. no public advisory required.

samir-kaur: follow-ups I'm putting in ticket: rotate any sibling tokens matching pattern, add TTL defaults to internal token issuance (max 24h), add rotate-on-detect automation that automatically revokes tokens flagged by scanner.

security-oncall: final: schedule postmortem in 3d, include OSS release lead, devex, and infra. root cause: secret left in publicized example. action items: automation for rotation, CI secret banlist, long-term audit, GH history purge process. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

opsbot: closing thread for now; update ticket #SE-2026-221 with results when done.
